title: Topological phases of a generalised tripartite Haldane model
authors: Ahmed Al-kharusi, Alessandro Principi, Niels R. Walet
abstract: We present a generalised tripartite Haldane model with a complex nearest neighbour hopping parameter. The total magnetic flux through the primitive unit cell, which consists of three hexagonal unit cells is zero, and thus the model has the structure of a loop-current model. We calculate topological phase diagrams of the Chern numbers as a function of the phases of the nearest and next-nearest neighbour hopping parameters for a fixed ratio of the magnitude of the hopping parameters. We show that, unlike the Haldane model, the topological phase diagram of this model is very complex, but some aspects can still be dealt with analytically. Furthermore, the Chern numbers of the topological phases are as large as $7$ in absolute value. The analysis is supported by explicit expressions for energy bands crossing at high symmetry points in the Brillouin zone, which show as linear phase boundaries in the phase diagram. We show that such lines explain many features in the topological phase diagrams. Finally, we analyse a few representative examples of the nature of level crossings away from high symmetry and their evolution with model parameters.
summary: This work analyzes the topological properties of a generalized tripartite Haldane model using a tight-binding Hamiltonian. By calculating the Chern number across a complex phase diagram, the authors demonstrate that the model supports much larger topological invariants than simpler analogues. The analysis relies heavily on identifying and characterizing the energy band crossings that define the phase boundaries.
main_problem: The paper investigates the topological phase diagram of a generalized tripartite Haldane model defined on a hexagonal lattice.
main_result: The model exhibits a highly complex topological phase diagram, with Chern numbers reaching absolute values as large as 7, significantly exceeding the simple values found in the original Haldane model.
method: Topological invariants (Chern numbers) are calculated by integrating the Berry curvature over the Brillouin zone, supported by analytical derivations of energy band crossings at high-symmetry points.
model_or_system: The system is described by a tight-binding Hamiltonian on a hexagonal lattice, forming a tripartite unit cell. The Hamiltonian incorporates complex nearest and next-nearest neighbor hopping parameters, and the analysis is based on diagonalizing a $6 	imes 6$ matrix.
key_observables: Chern number (C), energy bands ($E_n$), and the Berry curvature ($\Omega_n(k)$).
important_parameters: Phases of hopping parameters ($	heta, \phi$), and the ratio of hopping parameter magnitudes ($t_2/t_1$).
main_assumptions: The Chern number calculation requires the energy band of interest to be well separated from other bands ($\Delta E \geq 10^{-4}t_1$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model structure, the topological phase diagrams showing Chern numbers vs. parameter phases, and plots detailing energy band crossings both at high-symmetry points and away from them.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the model and its Hamiltonian, then details the numerical and analytical methods for calculating the Chern number. It systematically analyzes the phase diagram by deriving explicit analytical expressions for band crossings at high-symmetry points ($\gamma, k_\pm, k'_\pm$), which dictate the phase transitions.
why_interesting: The study of topological phases in lattice models, especially those involving complex hopping parameters and emergent loop currents, provides deep insights into the robustness of quantum states against perturbations, which is fundamental to topological quantum computing concepts.
